metadata.title: Trace It, Don't Fix It.
metadata.subtitle: The Break-Trace Skill (Reconciliation Audit Trail)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: when Claude finds a break in the books, does it fix the discrepancy, or just explain it? Lands the carry-out that break-trace finds exactly where two numbers stopped agreeing and says why — it never decides what happens next.

beats.narration_text: You'd assume Claude fixes a break in the books when it runs this skill. It doesn't — it traces one. So what does break-trace actually do, and why did they stop it short of the fix?

beats.narration_text: Here's what a skill actually is: a folder Claude reads before it works. Break-trace is one of them, and inside sits exactly one file — SKILL.md, written in plain English. No compiled code, no runtime magic, nothing hidden below the text. Claude reads the file, then does what it says. They chose readability over cleverness: the file is the program, so anyone who can read English can audit it.

Open the file and the instructions are steps — Claude runs them top to bottom, in order. Read the file, run each step exactly as written, hand back the result. No branching, unless a step itself says branch. That constraint is doing real work here: it's what makes the same input produce the same output, run after run. They optimized for repeatability at the expense of cleverness.

Break-trace only fires after another skill has already flagged a break — a spot where two records that should agree, don't. Its job: follow the trail back on each side to the original transaction or posting, then state exactly what's different and why. Notice what's missing from that list: it never decides what to do about the difference. That cut is deliberate. They optimized for auditability — you get the cause in plain language, and the fix stays yours.

production_viz.label: TRACE, NOT FIX
production_viz.caption: finds why, not what to fix

beats.narration_text: Break-trace lands exactly where two numbers stopped agreeing and says why — and it stops there. The fix stays yours. That cut is the whole design.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini — read it with me. I have two numbers that should match, but they don't. Before you try to fix anything, walk me through exactly where they first differ and why. Go deeper: once you've located the split, what would push you to trust one side over the other — and what signals in the trail would you look for? Liam, in for Bear.
